canonical_question: What specific Wyckoff positions are occupied by the Ti atoms in the C14 phase, and does the '2a, 4f, 6h' description match the standard C14 Laves structure?

question_variants.question: What specific Wyckoff positions are occupied by the Ti atoms in the C14 phase, and does the '2a, 4f, 6h' description match the standard C14 Laves structure?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The C14 Laves phase structure is confirmed to be hexagonal (space group P 6 3 / mmc, No. 194) comprising three inequivalent sites designated as 2a, 4f, and 6h. The text does not explicitly detail which Wyckoff positions are occupied by Ti atoms specifically, only the site designations available.

answers.answer: The C14 Laves phase adopts a hexagonal structure (space group: P 6 3 / mmc , No. 194), comprising three inequivalent sites with the 2 a , 4 f , and 6 h designations. The document does not specify the exact Ti occupancy among these sites.
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific Ti atom Wyckoff positions not explicitly defined in the provided text.
evidence_spans: We report the magnetic properties of the as-cast high-entropy alloy (HEA) FeCoNiTi, characterized by a dual phase comprising the face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
The HEA manifests three distinct ferromagnetic orderings at 1084, 214, and 168 K.
The emergence of the 214 K transition is attributed to the influence of the C14 phase.
